utility.name: LLM API relay
utility.author: Thomas Shaw
utility.description: An nginx reverse proxy that lets lab VMs on an isolated network use the local LLMs (an OpenAI-compatible API such as the Spark LLM gateway) without joining the internal network. Only the chat completions and model list endpoints are relayed, and the relay can add the API key itself so that no key is stored on a student VM. Clients use http://<relay IP>:<listen_port>/api/v1/ as their base URL (e.g. the ghidra module's llm_relay_ip input). The system needs an internal network as well as its lab network: add <network type="internal_network"/> to it. The module checks for it (the secgen_internal_network fact) and fails clearly without it. The relay is self-contained, including its firewall (nftables, loaded from the next boot, i.e. after the build): inbound only the relay port from the lab subnets (or allowed_networks) plus lab_inbound_ports, nothing new from the internal network, outbound only to the upstream API, DHCP and the lab subnets, and no forwarding. It therefore conflicts with the other firewall modules. Put it on a system students don't control (e.g. a dedicated VM, or the Hackerbot server with its ports in lab_inbound_ports). The API key normally comes from secgen.rb's llm-api-key option (e.g. in secgen.conf): the llm_api_key type below makes SecGen pass it as a Puppet fact read from the environment, so it is never written to the scenario or the generated project. It takes precedence over the api_key input, which is only for one-off testing (an api_key input ends up in the project files).
